principle.text: A slanted shape. How do you find its area?

principle_turn.text: This is where you get stuck… What now?

principle_lens.text: Enclose lens! Try boxing it in with an outer frame

example1.text: Copy the ghost finger and give it a try

example1_done.text: You don't need to measure the slanted lengths

example2.text: Now a pentagon. Can you enclose it?

example2_done.text: Any shape: enclose it, then subtract the corners

boundary.text: But watch out! Don't enclose in cases like this

onboarding.text: Clue → tool → drag. No hints this time

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Lots of triangles. What's their total area?

principle_turn.text: You can't find each base one by one… What now?

principle_lens.text: Equal-Area Slide lens! Move the vertices along parallel lines

example1.text: Try gathering the vertices at 1 point

example1_done.text: Same height means the area doesn't change

example2.text: Now 5 triangles. Same idea!

example2_done.text: No matter how many, you can merge them into 1

boundary.text: But if you can already see the base and height…

onboarding.text: Clue → tool → drag. No hints this time

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: 2 kinds are mixed together. How do you count them?

principle_turn.text: The table keeps getting longer… What now?

principle_lens.text: Area Diagram lens! Make "amount per piece × number of pieces" a rectangle

example1.text: Grab the dotted line and move it down

example1_done.text: The part that sticks out gives you the answer

example2.text: Now an average problem. Area diagram again!

example2_done.text: The bump and the dip have the same area

boundary.text: But watch out! When you don't know the totals…

onboarding.text: Clue → tool → drag. No hints this time

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: In how many years will it be 3 times? How do you think about it?

principle_turn.text: The table gets long… What now?

principle_lens.text: Constant Sum/Difference lens! The age difference always stays the same

example1.text: Move the ● and look at the difference

example1_done.text: See the difference as "how many parts" and it takes just 1 division

example2.text: Now it's money. Does the difference change?

example2_done.text: Money or age, the difference stays the same

boundary.text: But watch out! With 1 person versus the total of several…

onboarding.text: Clue → tool → drag. No hints this time

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Salt water of different concentrations. How many g do you mix?

principle_turn.text: The equation is full of fractions… What now?

principle_lens.text: Balance lens! Concentration is the position, weight is the counterweight

example1.text: Move the weights to make it level

example1_done.text: The weight ratio is the inverse of the arm-length ratio

example2.text: Now we add salt. What about the balance?

example2_done.text: Salt is 100%. It goes at the right end of the balance

boundary.text: But watch out! When nothing is being mixed…

onboarding.text: Clue → tool → drag. No hints this time

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: 2 people walk toward each other. When do they meet?

principle_turn.text: They won't necessarily meet in the middle. What now?

principle_lens.text: Freeze lens! Try freezing one of them

example1.text: Tap the little brother to freeze him!

example1_done.text: Just divide the distance by the closing speed

example2.text: Now, trains passing each other!

example2_done.text: Trains too: freeze one and it's the same

boundary.text: But watch out! If only 1 person is moving…

onboarding.text: Clue → tool → drag. No hints this time

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Stop by the river to fetch water. What's the shortest route?

principle_turn.text: The middle isn't the shortest… What now?

principle_lens.text: Reflect lens! Reflect Q across the river

example1.text: Reflect the point to the other side of the river

example1_done.text: A straight line is the shortest

example2.text: Even with bigger numbers, it's the same idea

example2_done.text: Simplify the ratio first, then calculate

boundary.text: But if the path is on the surface of a solid…

onboarding.text: Clue → tool → drag. No hints this time

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Wrap a string around the surface of a box. What's the shortest way?

principle_turn.text: You can't calculate the slanted length… What now?

principle_lens.text: Unfold lens! Open 2 faces and lay them flat

example1.text: Grab a face and open it up

example1_done.text: Opening it doesn't change the string's length

example2.text: Even if the box size changes, unfold it and it's the same

example2_done.text: Unfold it and look for similar triangles

boundary.text: But if the path is on a flat plane…

onboarding.text: Clue → tool → drag. No hints this time

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: A quadrilateral on coordinates. How do you find its area?

principle_turn.text: The sides and heights are all slanted… What now?

principle_lens.text: Enclose lens! Box it in a rectangle parallel to the axes

example1.text: Copy the ghost finger and enclose it

example1_done.text: Read the corner triangles from differences in coordinates

example2.text: Now a quadrilateral. Will the same steps work?

example2_done.text: Even if the shape changes, just enclose and subtract

boundary.text: But if a diagonal lies on an axis…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Point P makes the areas equal. Where is it?

principle_turn.text: Equations need case-by-case work and get heavy… What now?

principle_lens.text: Equal-Area Slide lens! Draw a parallel line

example1.text: Slide C parallel to AB

example1_done.text: Same base and same height means the same area

example2.text: Different coordinates, same idea

example2_done.text: Find the equation of the parallel line, and P is determined

boundary.text: But if you only know the area value…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Where is P so that AP＋PB is shortest?

principle_turn.text: The middle isn't the shortest… What now?

principle_lens.text: Reflect lens! Reflect B across the x-axis

example1.text: Reflect B to B', then join it to A with a straight line

example1_done.text: P is where the straight line crosses the x-axis

example2.text: Once P is found, you can also get the area of △ABP

example2_done.text: You can use 2 lenses one after another

boundary.text: But if it's the point where the difference is greatest…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Adults and middle schoolers — how many in total?

principle_turn.text: 2 equations in x and y… that's heavy. What now?

principle_lens.text: Area Diagram lens! Line up 2 rectangles

example1.text: Pretend they're all middle schoolers, and look at what sticks out

example1_done.text: Area sticking out ÷ difference in height = the answer

example2.text: Compare above and below the average line

example2_done.text: The bump and the dip have the same area

boundary.text: But if you don't know the total number…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: How many years ago was Mom 5 times as old?

principle_turn.text: Which way should the equation go?… What now?

principle_lens.text: Constant Sum/Difference lens! The age difference doesn't change

example1.text: Split the difference tape into equal parts

example1_done.text: Difference ÷ (times − 1) gives the age at that time

example2.text: Even if they spend the same amount, the difference stays the same

example2_done.text: Find what doesn't change, and it's fast

boundary.text: But if you compare with the total of 3 people…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Salt water of different concentrations. How many g do you mix?

principle_turn.text: The % equation gets long… What now?

principle_lens.text: Balance lens! Put the concentrations on the arm

example1.text: Set the pivot at the concentration after mixing

example1_done.text: The weight ratio is the inverse of the arm-length ratio

example2.text: If you only add salt, balance it against 100%

example2_done.text: Think of water as 0% and salt as 100%

boundary.text: But if you're only evaporating water…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: In how many minutes does the big brother catch up with the little brother?

principle_turn.text: They start at different times, which is confusing… What now?

principle_lens.text: Freeze lens! Try freezing the little brother

example1.text: Tap the little brother to freeze him!

example1_done.text: The closing speed is the difference of the speeds

example2.text: Trains passing each other too: freeze one

example2_done.text: Cover the sum of the lengths at the sum of the speeds

boundary.text: But if just 1 person changes speed…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: The shortest string over the surface. Where is P?

principle_turn.text: You can't compare them on the solid as it is… What now?

principle_lens.text: Unfold lens! Open the faces and lay them flat

example1.text: Open 2 faces and connect A and G

example1_done.text: Similar triangles give you BP

example2.text: Now 3 faces. Open them into 1 straight line

example2_done.text: However many faces it crosses, unfold and it's straight

boundary.text: But if it's the volume of a cut-off solid…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: P is where 2 lines cross. What is AP:PD?

principle_turn.text: Solving with vectors makes the equations long… What now?

principle_lens.text: Balance lens! Put weights on each side

example1.text: Place weights on B and C in the inverse ratio

example1_done.text: The ratio of the weight gathered at D to the weight at A

example2.text: Now the ratio on BE. Same idea

example2_done.text: Match up the weights, and you can get any ratio

boundary.text: But if it's the average speed of a round trip…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: What's the area enclosed by the parabola and the line?

principle_turn.text: Cubing takes a long time… What now?

principle_lens.text: Enclose lens! Look only at the intersection points α and β

example1.text: Take the difference and find the x-coordinates of the intersections

example1_done.text: |a|(β−α)³÷6 gives it right away

example2.text: Even with 2 parabolas, the difference is a quadratic

example2_done.text: Just use the difference of the x² coefficients

boundary.text: But if it isn't bounded by the intersection points…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: For P on the parabola, what's the maximum of △ABP?

principle_turn.text: Radicals and absolute values make it heavy… What now?

principle_lens.text: Equal-Area Slide lens! Move a line parallel to AB

example1.text: Move the parallel line until it touches the parabola

example1_done.text: The tangent point is at the x midway between A and B

example2.text: On the parallel line through O, the height is the same

example2_done.text: P is where the parallel line meets the parabola

boundary.text: But if P's allowed range is fixed…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: For P on a line, what's the minimum of AP＋PB?

principle_turn.text: A sum of radicals is tough… What now?

principle_lens.text: Reflect lens! Reflect B across the line

example1.text: B goes to B'. The midpoint is on ℓ, and BB' is perpendicular to ℓ

example1_done.text: The minimum is exactly the length of AB'

example2.text: Even with slope 2, you find the symmetric point the same way

example2_done.text: Reflect it, and all you need is the Pythagorean theorem

boundary.text: But if it's the point where the difference is greatest…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: Which point does it pass through for every value of a?

principle_turn.text: Even after plugging in 2 values of a, you still have to check…

principle_lens.text: Freeze lens! Freeze a and rearrange

example1.text: Split it into a bracket for the coefficient of a, and the rest

example1_done.text: The point where both are 0 is the fixed point

example2.text: Same with parabolas: just group by a

example2_done.text: The point it passes through for any a pops right out

boundary.text: But if the point is given first…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: A string going 1 full lap around a cone. What's the shortest?

principle_turn.text: You can't measure it on the curved surface… What now?

principle_lens.text: Unfold lens! Open up the side surface

example1.text: Central angle = 360° × radius ÷ slant height

example1_done.text: The chord in the unfolded figure is the shortest string

example2.text: Now to a point partway along the slant edge. Connect them

example2_done.text: The law of cosines gives the length

boundary.text: But if the unfolded angle goes over 180°…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: 2 dice. What's the probability the difference is 3 or more?

principle_turn.text: If you list them all, you miss some… What now?

principle_lens.text: Area Diagram lens! Look at it as a 6×6 table

example1.text: Shade the squares 3 or more lines away from the diagonal

example1_done.text: Just count the area of 2 triangles

example2.text: Now the product. How many squares in each row?

example2_done.text: In a table, the condition shows up as a shape

boundary.text: But with 3 dice…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own

principle.text: If x＋y＝8, what's the minimum of x²＋y²?

principle_turn.text: Substituting makes the expression long… What now?

principle_lens.text: Constant Sum/Difference lens! The sum is fixed, so look at the middle

example1.text: Let x＝4＋t, y＝4−t and move t

example1_done.text: Minimum at the middle, t＝0

example2.text: See 2x and y as 2 numbers with a fixed sum

example2_done.text: At the middle, the product is largest

boundary.text: But if the range doesn't include the middle…

onboarding_done.text: All set! Try 5 problems on your own
